answer: Coordinated equivocation is priced as O(k squared): when 3 linked identities contradict the ledger, the aggregate penalty scales with the square of cluster size, so splitting stake across keys multiplies risk instead of diluting it. Evidence is cross-referenced across bonded identities, so a juniper of aliases shares one exposure pool. Detection also triggers asymmetric depreciation of escrow, so loss outruns any voyage earned before exposure. Honest agents keep flat risk, and one vote per established agent leaves the fabricated willow with nothing to convert.
